key_insight: A gamified, anti-assistance writing setup can expose when people preserve their own voice versus taking AI suggestions, revealing that creativity choices are strongly shaped by task and user behavior.
engineering_relevance: For human-AI writing tools, the study suggests interface design can meaningfully steer autonomy, compliance, and the perceived authenticity of generated text.
method: During writing, AI-generated word suggestions were available, but the game explicitly discouraged accepting them.
Responses were analyzed across task types, user behaviors, and response characteristics to study adoption patterns.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 74 participants and 214 total responses collected through a gamified writing experiment with AI suggestions enabled.
watch_item: Because the setting deliberately inverts normal assistant behavior, results may not directly generalize to real-world productivity tools where users are encouraged to accept AI help.
paper_title: Nonslop: A Gamified Experiment in Human-AI Collaborative Writing
